title: How do we turn four big fractions into decimals?
description: Four fractions are each given a bottom of ten, a hundred or a thousand by multiplying the top and the bottom by the same number. The result is read as a decimal. A long division checks the first fraction.
teaching_notes: One idea: choose the number that makes each bottom ten, a hundred or a thousand, and multiply the top and the bottom by it. Watch for students who multiply only the bottom.

video_script.why: The child can share by place value but has not chosen the multiplier that makes each bottom ten, a hundred or a thousand.
video_script.substitution: Each bottom is turned into ten, a hundred or a thousand by multiplying top and bottom alike, and a long division checks it.
video_script.anchor: Eighteen fifths, four hundred and fifteen quarters, twelve hundred and seventeen halves and forty eight twenty seven eighths
video_script.payoff_line: Four thousand eight hundred and twenty seven over eight is six hundred and three point three seven five.

final_answer.spoken: three point six, a hundred and three point seven five, six hundred and eight point five and six hundred and three point three seven five

video_script.fraction_reading: A fraction such as 18/5 is read eighteen over five, 415/4 is four hundred and fifteen over four, 1217/2 is one thousand two hundred and seventeen over two, 4827/8 is four thousand eight hundred and twenty seven over eight, and 603375/1000 is six hundred and three thousand three hundred and seventy five over a thousand.
maths_rules: check by long division: 18 Ones / 5 = 3 Ones rem 3; 30 Tenths / 5 = 6 Tenths, so 3.6
video_script.design: The four fractions stay on the board; each line of the solution turns one bottom into ten, a hundred or a thousand, and a long division closes the loop.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; four fractions side by side: 18/5, 415/4, 1217/2, 4827/8, each with an empty decimal box

marks.last: the last two fractions appear one by one

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about dividing into a decimal.
<bookmark mark='first'/>The first two are eighteen over five and four hundred and fifteen over four.
<bookmark mark='last'/>The next is one thousand two hundred and seventeen over two. The last is four thousand eight hundred and twenty seven over eight.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What are these four fractions as decimals?

beats.on_screen: the four fractions and their empty boxes stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: Bottoms 5, 4, 2 and 8 are matched to 10, 100 and 1000; multiply top and bottom by the same number; a long division frame waits at the side

marks.same: an arrow links the bottoms to ten, a hundred or a thousand
marks.rule: the words top and bottom, same number are written
marks.div: a long division frame appears at the side

narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>We solve this the same way as the example in your book. First make each bottom ten, a hundred or a thousand.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>Multiply the top and the bottom by the same number, so the fraction stays equal.
<bookmark mark='div'/>Then a long division will check one of the answers.

marks.given: the first two fractions are written
marks.given2: the last two fractions are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, four fractions. Eighteen over five and four hundred and fifteen over four. <bookmark mark='given2'/>One thousand two hundred and seventeen over two and four thousand eight hundred and twenty seven over eight.

beats.on_screen: To find: each fraction as a decimal, and check it by long division

marks.find: the four decimal boxes and a check box are outlined

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to write each fraction as a decimal, and then check one by long division.
<bookmark mark='s1a'/>Step one, eighteen over five, where five times two is ten.
<bookmark mark='s1b'/>Multiply the top and the bottom by two. We get thirty six over ten.
<bookmark mark='s1c'/>Thirty six over ten is three point six.
<bookmark mark='s2a'/>Step two, four hundred and fifteen over four, where four times twenty five is a hundred.
<bookmark mark='s2b'/>Multiply the top and the bottom by twenty five. We get ten thousand three hundred and seventy five over a hundred.
<bookmark mark='s2c'/>That is a hundred and three point seven five.
<bookmark mark='s3a'/>Step three, one thousand two hundred and seventeen over two, where two times five is ten.
<bookmark mark='s3b'/>Multiply the top and the bottom by five. We get six thousand and eighty five over ten.
<bookmark mark='s3c'/>That is six hundred and eight point five.

marks.s4c: 603375/1000 is written with the decimal left blank

narration: <bookmark mark='s4a'/>Step four, four thousand eight hundred and twenty seven over eight. Eight times a hundred and twenty five is a thousand.
<bookmark mark='s4b'/>Multiply the top and the bottom by a hundred and twenty five.
<bookmark mark='s4c'/>We get six hundred and three thousand three hundred and seventy five over a thousand.

beats.on_screen: Check: 18 ÷ 5 by long division: 18 Ones ÷ 5 = 3 Ones, 3 Ones remain; 3 Ones = 30 Tenths; 30 Tenths ÷ 5 = 6 Tenths; 3.6 matches

marks.s5a: 18 ÷ 5 is set in the long division frame and three Ones go to the answer
marks.s5b: the three Ones that remain regroup into thirty Tenths
marks.s5c: six Tenths go to the answer and it matches 3.6

narration: <bookmark mark='s5a'/>Step five, check the first one by long division. Eighteen Ones divided by five gives three Ones.
<bookmark mark='s5b'/>Three Ones remain. Regroup them into thirty Tenths.
<bookmark mark='s5c'/>Thirty Tenths divided by five gives six Tenths. That matches three point six.

marks.rest: the other three decimals are boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Four thousand eight hundred and twenty seven over eight is six hundred and three point three seven five.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>The other three are three point six and six hundred and eight point five. The second is a hundred and three point seven five.
